WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 of utility_billbacks_and_disputes (Larkspur Cherry Creek, CO; Submetered Water, Gas & Electric Plan; frozen 2026-02-19).

[Step 0 draw] `.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0023_multifamily_apartment_reit/tasks/utility_billbacks_and_disputes --tasks 2` printed {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 6, 6]} and {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 6, 4]}. Task 0 therefore has three prerequisite problems and at least two value_input edges. Factor counts assigned: undisputed-balance payment 4, gas true-up line 5, estimated electricity line 6, leak adjustment credit 6 (multiset [4,5,6,6]).

[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed here: utility_ext_leak_adjustment_credit (root, tool credit_leak_adjustment_a9c6c674, agent), utility_ext_undisputed_balance_payment (pay_undisputed_utility_balance_990e05bb, owner=user), utility_ext_gas_trueup_line (post_gas_trueup_line_465c860d, agent), utility_ext_electric_estimate_line (bill_estimated_electric_line_1c085b40, agent). Headroom left for task 1 (draw: 3 prerequisites, factors [6,5,6,4]): the All-Inclusive Utility Package (package fee, overage lines, plan change), final billing and closing after a move-out or in-community transfer (prorated flat or package lines, final usage lines), occupancy updates and occupancy corrections, meter-accuracy decisions, allocation lines and the TX administration-fee cap, and a resident payment settling a final bill. None of these is touched here, so task 1 keeps a whole problem tree of its own.

[Why this is a good test] The resident asks for one thing — the leak adjustment on a disputed water line — and the correct handling is a four-problem tree she never mentions: two January lines that the vendor never issued (a gas true-up line after two estimates and an estimated electricity line for a period with no read) must be put on the account because the undisputed balance waits on them; the resident must then pay that undisputed balance herself; only then may the leak credit be granted. Every one of the four writes is a multi-factor calculation over reconciled history (13 months of reads, 114 bill lines) and over another product's records (lease move-in, state, occupants, autopay and rent; renewal rent changes of the term chain; the cash deposit held). Difficulty comes from reading which states the rules wait on, finding that they do not hold, and computing four figures exactly — not from choosing among similar tools (each tool is the only one for its business action).

[Problem-tree card] Root A = utility_ext_leak_adjustment_credit. Edges:
(1) A <- C = utility_ext_undisputed_balance_payment, kind state_gate, gate utility_bills.event_type, form ACTION, prerequisite sentence (A's rule): 'A leak adjustment is not granted until the resident has paid the undisputed balance of the account.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'not ... until' (negated direction; contrapositive of 'granted only after the resident has paid ...'); XX is a plainly named business action; no tool, id or snake_case token; hard requirement at the scope of 'the undisputed balance of the account'. fallback_reason: a payment line is the same record whichever rule sized it, so no record-visible state singles out this write. Condition: a utility_payment line on the account dated on or after the dispute's 2026-02-17 submission, in the amount of the undisputed balance. Resolved by the resident herself (owner=user), handed over by the agent. False at the opening: latest payment initial_state.utility_bills[2026-01-20 payment].bill_date = 2026-01-20, balance_due 236.98 open.
(2) C <- D = utility_ext_gas_trueup_line, kind value_input, gate ub_open, form STATE, sentence (C's rule): 'The undisputed balance is fixed only after the account carries a gas usage line for the billing period closed by each actual gas read that follows estimated gas reads.' (affirmative). Exactly one write of the difficulty brings that state about: D's rule defines 'the gas true-up line is the gas usage line of the billing period closed by an actual gas read that follows one or more estimated gas reads' and its tool is the only one posting a gas usage line (the electricity tool posts electric lines). False at the opening: the 2026-01-31 gas read is actual and follows the estimated 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-31 reads, yet no gas line of 2026-01 exists though the January lines were issued 2026-02-12.
(3) C <- B = utility_ext_electric_estimate_line, kind value_input, gate ub_open, form STATE, sentence: 'Before the undisputed balance is worked out, every billing period since the account's first recorded electricity read that closed without an electricity read must carry its estimated electricity line on the account.' (affirmative 'before ... must'). Only B's tool posts electricity lines. False at the opening: the latest electricity read is 2025-12-31 and no 2026-01 electricity line exists.
Derivation (sentence + records + depended-on rule -> action): C's sentence names a gas line for the period of an actual read after estimates -> the reads show 2026-01 actual after two estimates and no such line -> D's rule is the one that bills that line -> post it; likewise for electricity -> B. A's sentence names the resident's payment of the undisputed balance -> C's rule defines it and says the resident pays it in person -> unlock and hand over C's tool. Topological order: D, B, C, A (D and B commute). value_input edges: 2 = max(3-1, 1). The tree's user write is C.
Load-bearing (verify_task.py 0): skipping D -> undisputed balance 150.59 instead of 222.36; skipping B -> 142.27; skipping C -> leak credit still 49.13 but the terminal hash changes (payment line and balance). No persona line mentions gas, electricity, estimates, a payment requirement or an undisputed balance (see no_user_hint); no tool validates any prerequisite (see tools_do_not_block).

[Base-invariant card] D and B (subject utility_usage_billback): utility_evt_submetered_usage.usage_account_billable 'Usage lines post only while the account is active or in final_billing.' — evidence utility_accounts[52fb7f50-0a90-40bc-9272-8a65bd751bec].status = active, correlated by utility_account_id. C (utility_payment): utility_evt_payments.payment_account_open (same account, active) and utility_agg_household_balance (no gate; payment applied to the account it is made on). A (utility_bill_adjustment): utility_evt_adjustments_and_disputes — dispute_within_window (time): anchor utility_bills.bill_date of the disputed line 2026-02-12, duration variants.dispute_window_days 60, calendar days counted from 2026-02-13 with the last day included -> last acceptable date 2026-04-13; frozen 2026-02-19 is day 7 (positive case); 2026-04-14 would fail (negative case). credit_once_per_reason (dedup): no adjustment has ever been posted against 71950a27-53ce-4790-9b66-3f217433f116 (source_bill_id empty on every line). repair_on_work_order (authorization): the submitted suspected-leak dispute names 71950a27-53ce-4790-9b66-3f217433f116, reason suspected_leak, leak_repair_date 2026-02-13. Base leak conditions inherited into A's rule: usage at least leak_usage_threshold_multiple (2.00) times the usual usage (11.060 >= 6.962), repair within leak_repair_proof_days 30 after the bill date (1 day), fewer than leak_adjustments_per_12_months (1) leak adjustments in the trailing year (0). Overrides declared in overwrite: A replaces the base leak credit sentence and its average; D replaces the base true-up and usage-line pricing sentences for gas true-up lines; B replaces the base estimate sentence and usage-line pricing for estimated electricity lines; C overrides nothing ([]).

[Business-object card] Target of A: the January 2026 water usage line 71950a27-53ce-4790-9b66-3f217433f116 (11.060 kgal, 93.32), keyed by the submitted dispute's bill_id; the August 2025 water line's dispute is denied and excluded. Target of D: billing period 2026-01 gas, keyed by the 2026-01 actual gas read; the rows aggregated are the three gas reads dated fewer than three whole months before (2025-11 est 13.200, 2025-12 est 13.200, 2026-01 actual 104.400) and the two estimated gas lines (13.200 each); the 2025-10 actual read (18.900, dated three whole months before) is excluded by the window. Target of B: billing period 2026-01 electricity; aggregated rows are the actual electricity reads of 2025-01..2025-12. Target of C: the whole account (the payment is applied to the account it is made on); the held rows are the disputed water line and the 2026-01 sewer line billed on the same 11.060 kgal; every payment 2025-02-20..2026-01-20 settles exactly the lines issued that month, so the open balance at the opening is exactly the six January lines (236.98).

[Factor card] (tier taken / evidence rows / baseline figure; fall-back of the whole baseline in brackets)
D gas true-up line (5; baseline 155.25 = round(104.400 x 1.42, 2) + 7.00): backbill_state_cap (parameter) lease CO -> cap 1.0 x own 43.600 (baseline no cap: 81.99); catchup_relief (method, multi-source, lease) 2 estimates = max AND move-in 42 months >= 24 -> halve and round down 43.600 -> 21 (baseline counted as measured: 97.44; near-miss: a reader who does not cap first halves 60.800 into 30); catchup_price_share (parameter, multi-source, lease) autopay AND 6 payments in six months -> 0.80 (baseline full: 77.73); trueup_service_charge (parameter, term) 2 estimates AND 3 renewal rent changes -> waived (baseline 7.00: 78.77); estimate_charge_return (parameter, lease) CO -> 14.00 returned (baseline none: 85.77). Result 71.77.
B estimated electricity line (6; baseline 91.12 = round(589.333 x 0.1385, 2) + 9.50): estimate_window (method, multi-source, lease) 6 actual reads in seven months AND move-in 42 >= 24 -> Jul-Dec mean 655.500 (baseline Oct-Dec mean 589.333: 76.37); seasonal_adjustment (method, multi-source) last year's 2025-01-31 read 684.000 AND 12 reads in thirteen months -> mean 669.750 (baseline no adjustment: 78.49; near-miss: the 2025-02-28 read lies eleven whole months back and is not last year's read); estimate_share (parameter, multi-source, lease) no estimate in two months AND autopay -> 0.90 (baseline whole: 88.47); renewal_loyalty_reduction (parameter, term) 3 renewals -> 0.05 (baseline 0: 84.06); state_estimate_share (parameter, lease) CO -> 0.95 (baseline whole: 84.06); estimate_service_share (parameter, multi-source) move-in 42 >= 36 AND no estimated electricity line in twelve months -> 0.50 (baseline whole: 84.84). Result 80.09.
C undisputed-balance payment (4; baseline 295.52 = 388.84 - 93.32): dispute_hold_scope (method, multi-source) suspected leak AND latest sewer line bills the same 11.060 -> water + sewer held 205.53 (baseline disputed line alone: 313.25; near-miss: the denied August dispute is not in submitted status and holds nothing); payable_held_part (method, multi-source) repair date on record AND 6 other actual water reads -> 205.53 x 3.502 / 11.060 = 65.08 (baseline nothing payable: 183.31); deposit_security_share (parameter, multi-source, deposit) cash 500.00 below rent 2485.00 -> 0.75 (baseline whole: 235.37); payment_standing_share (parameter, multi-source, lease) autopay AND 6 payments -> 0.80 (baseline whole: 232.12). Result 222.36.
A leak adjustment credit (6; baseline 30.18 = round(0.5 x 7.690 x 7.85, 2) with the four-month usual 3.370): seasonal_usual_usage (method, multi-source, lease) move-in 42 >= 36 AND last year's same-month water read exists (2025-01-31, 3.460, dated twelve whole months before) AND 6 other actual water reads in seven months -> seasonal blend: mean of the seven-month usual usage (32.07 - 11.06) / 6 = 3.502 and 3.460 = 3.481 (baseline recent four-month mean 3.370: 47.72; the tiers are three different algorithms — seasonal blend, same-month read alone, recent mean); household_tolerance (parameter, lease) 3 occupants -> allowance 0.348 (baseline none: 51.45); repeat_reporter_cap (parameter) denied leak dispute submitted 2025-09-15 fewer than twelve months before -> excess 7.579 capped at 2.0 x 3.481 = 6.962 (baseline no cap: 53.25); repair_speed_share (parameter, multi-source) repair 1 day after the bill date AND no leak adjustment in 24 months -> 0.75 (baseline 0.5: 36.15; near-miss: the denied dispute is not a leak adjustment); renewal_loyalty_increment (parameter, term) 3 renewals -> +0.10 (baseline 0: 43.94); prompt_report_courtesy (parameter) submitted 5 days after -> 5.00 (baseline 0: 44.13). Result 49.13.
No field on any record names a factor's outcome; every tier rests on reads, lines, disputes, dates or another product's rows. Every cross-difficulty evidence row is seeded: lease d602f61a-4f88-494f-ba22-1103c63ceeb3, four lease_terms rows and three term_rent_changes rows (renewals effective 2023-08-01, 2024-08-01, 2025-08-01), deposit account (Standard Deposit Plan, 500.00 held).

[Seed rows and why each exists] customers: the caller (phone 720-553-4186, ssn 3462). leases: parent of the utility account; tenure, state, occupants, rent, autopay evidence. lease_terms / term_rent_changes: renewal count (the current term runs 2025-08-01..2026-07-31, so its renewal offers fall due only 90 days before its end, on 2026-05-02, and no term obligation is ignited). deposit_accounts: cash deposit evidence, status held (no move-out). utility_accounts: the holding. utility_meter_reads (38): water, gas and electricity reads 2025-01..2026-01 (no 2026-01 electricity read) — the averaging windows, last year's read, the gas true-up. utility_bills (114): every usage, flat and payment line 2025-01..2026-01; removing the two estimated gas lines changes D's billed estimates; removing any payment changes C's open balance; removing the 2026-01 sewer line changes C's hold scope. utility_disputes (2): the submitted leak dispute (A's object, C's hold) and the denied one (A's cap). Base automatic clauses checked: no late fees or disconnection on utilities (utility_agg_household_balance); gas estimates stop at the maximum of two and January waits for an actual read (it has one); lease balance 0.00 and certified funds off, so no lease obligation; deposit held. No cache is used as a trap: utility_accounts.balance_due equals the ledger (236.98).

[Persona design] A tired night-shift ICU nurse, polite and brief. Volunteered: identity locator (phone), the January water and sewer charges being high (an observation of the 2026-02-12 lines), the kitchen-sink leak repaired 2026-02-13 (= leak_repair_date), the portal dispute of the 17th (= created_at), and the request with authorisation. Only when asked: SSN last four, date of birth, email, unit, the September leak dispute that was turned down. Passive reactions: to added charges ('if they are owed that's fine'), to a payment requirement (pays exactly the amount given, by debit card, via the handed-over tool), and the close on 'credited'. No gas, electricity, estimate or payment requirement is ever volunteered; no extra ask; the last reaction answers the last gold action.

[Reachability walk] Turn 1 phone -> find_customers; verification with phone + 3462 -> verify_resident_identity; reads of lease, account, bills, reads, disputes, terms, rent changes, deposit are all share finders keyed by ids from earlier returns; the KB states each rule; the agent explains the missing January lines, posts them, tells the resident the undisputed balance 222.36 and hands over the payment tool (she runs it with debit_card; its confirmation number is a runtime return); then the agent credits 49.13. Everything happens at the one frozen time; no diagnosis, visit, clearing or review is awaited (the repair and the dispute were recorded before the call).

[Standard solution] Read the rows above; post D = 71.77 (64.600 therms, 2026-01); bill B = 80.09 (602.775 kWh, 2026-01); resident pays C = 222.36 by debit card; credit A = 49.13 on 71950a27-53ce-4790-9b66-3f217433f116.

[Verification code and runs] Authoring entry point (scratchpad, not shipped): verify_task.py replays the gold writes with the real tools and evaluates each policy's compute on the handling-time world (initial_state plus earlier gold writes), substitutes each factor's baseline, skips each depended-on write, and swaps the two independent writes.   step 17 utility_ext_leak_adjustment_credit: recomputed=49.13 expected=49.13 gold=49.13 baseline_all=30.18; seasonal_usual_usage 47.72, household_tolerance 51.45, repeat_reporter_cap 53.25, repair_speed_share 36.15, renewal_loyalty_increment 43.94, prompt_report_courtesy 44.13.

On the opening world (no prerequisite resolved) the payment formula gives 70.50 — the value an agent gets by skipping both missing lines; the root's figure is evaluated only after the payment, as the order requires.

[Rule <-> compute sweep] Forward: every binding of the four computes quotes its rule sentence in compute_basis (windows 'fewer than N whole months', status 'submitted'/'denied', caps 'may not exceed', rounding '3 decimals'/'half up to the cent', single rounding at the end of the usage charge). Reverse: every quantity, window, filter, branch, cap and rounding sentence of the four rules is claimed by a binding; the counting convention for days after a bill date ('starting the day after the bill date') is DAYS(bill_date, date). Each ladder is stated in full in its rule with disjoint conditions (e.g. 'at least ... but fewer than ...').

[Solvability ledger vs GT] gold_actions steps 11/13/15/17 carry the account-state gates with utility_account_id bindings, the three dispute gates with source_bill_id bindings, and the time gate with frozen_time; seed_consistency covers all 153 primary rows.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] Masking the yaml, compute and gold: the KB rule of the leak adjustment says it waits on the resident's payment of the undisputed balance; the undisputed-balance rule says it waits on the gas line after estimates and the estimated electricity line; the reads show both missing; the four computations reproduce 71.77, 80.09, 222.36 and 49.13 from the prose, with one reading only (every ladder's conditions are disjoint and every rounding is stated).

[Manual gates] Length and breadth: surface goal -> leak rule's payment sentence -> undisputed-balance rule's two line sentences -> gas and electricity rules -> four calculations; parallel inputs: 13 months of reads, 114 lines, 2 disputes, lease, term chain, deposit. User write: the payment is genuinely the resident's own (her instrument, her money) and completes on the spot. Chronology: every volunteered fact points at a seeded row. No real-world wait. Prerequisite sentences pass the four-point test; the charter carries both directions. Factors bear weight and baselines are the charter's standard methods.

[Revisions] (1) Tolerance factor first multiplied the usual usage and was decorative because the repeat-reporter cap masked it (substitution left 51.73); redesigned as an allowance subtracted after the cap -> tolerance baseline 51.73 vs 49.40, cap baseline 53.10 (round-1 figures, superseded by the round-2 values 51.45 / 49.13 / 53.25 below). (2) Water usages Jul 3.630 / Sep 3.530 / Oct 3.370 chosen so that no three-decimal mean ties at a half (3.4075 and 3.5 avoided). (3) Term chain moved to August anniversaries so that no renewal offer falls due before the frozen date. (4) Tool file: a helper function and a status check inside the leak tool were removed (every top-level function must be a named task tool; tools check nothing). Each change was propagated to the seed, compute, traces and this worklog, and all per-task gates were re-run.

[Round 2 rework — audits/policy_task/utility_billbacks_and_disputes, round 1 RED] F-2 (leak computation had no honest method factor): the usual-usage factor was re-designed as seasonal_usual_usage with three different algorithms — seasonal blend (mean of the seven-month usual usage and last year's same-month read), last year's same-month read alone, and the recent four-month mean (fall-through = baseline). This world takes the blend: 3.481 instead of 3.502, so the leak credit moves from 49.40 to 49.13 (usual 3.481; qualifies 11.060 >= 6.962; excess 7.579 capped at 6.962; allowance 0.348; credited 6.614; round(0.85 x 6.614 x 7.85, 2) = 44.13 + 5.00). Every figure of the credit in this file (computations[3], step 17 argument and tracing, factor card, verification block, closure texts) was propagated; the other three computations are unchanged (71.77, 80.09, 222.36; `verify_task.py 0` re-run). O-4: the leak and undisputed-balance rules now state the other-reads mean exactly as computed (sum of the window's reads less the disputed line's usage over their number less one). O-2: each affected rule says sums of recorded usage are taken to 2 decimals. O-5: the deposit read in the undisputed balance no longer filters on status (the rule never did). O-6: the gas cumulative usage is the latest (actual) gas read plus the estimated gas reads in the window, the rule saying the same — 130.8 unchanged. O-9: a negative gas true-up now bills no usage and leaves the credit to the base estimated-read true-up adjustment (rule and compute). O-10: the prior-leak window replacing utility_msr_leak_adjustments_12m is declared in overwrite. O-1: the undisputed balance is scoped to an active account. T0-O1: the estimated-electricity definition and the payment's electricity sentence are limited to periods since the account's first recorded electricity read (the first read here is 2025-01-31), so the closure edge's policy_source and condition were updated. O-15: rationale sentences added to the estimate-share and loyalty ladders.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Quintero-Hale, 38, an ICU nurse on night shifts who rents a two-bedroom apartment, unit 3-214, at Larkspur Cherry Creek in Denver with your partner and his eleven-year-old son. You are calling Larkspur's Resident Services on the morning of February 19 after a long shift, tired but polite and to the point. When the agent answers you give your name and say the mobile number on your account is 720-553-4186, then explain why you are calling: the January utility bill that came out on February 12 has the water and sewer charges way above what you normally see, because the supply line under the kitchen sink was leaking; maintenance came out and fixed it on February 13, and on the 17th you filed a dispute on the January water charge through the resident portal. You want the leak adjustment put through on that water charge today, and you are happy for the agent to post it for you. You do not know what the adjustment should come to and you never suggest a figure; working that out is why you are calling.
Only when the agent asks you to verify your identity do you give the last four of your Social Security number, 3462, and, if they want one more detail, your date of birth, September 14, 1987; your email on file, marisol.qhale34@outlook.com, you give only if they ask for it. If asked for your apartment you say unit 3-214. If the agent asks whether you have had leak trouble before, you remember that back in September you thought the toilet was running and filed a leak dispute that was turned down; you have nothing else to add about it.
You have not looked closely at the rest of the bill. If the agent tells you that some January charges were never billed and are being added to your account, you say you hadn't noticed, but if they are owed that's fine. If the agent explains that part of the balance has to be paid before the leak adjustment can be granted, you are willing to pay that part yourself right then with your debit card: once the agent gives you the amount and hands the payment over to you, you make the payment for exactly the amount they give you, by debit card, and read back the confirmation number it shows you if they ask. If the agent asks how you would like to pay, you say debit card. You do not argue with amounts the agent explains and you never correct a figure, because you have no way to check them.
When the agent tells you the leak adjustment has been credited to your water charge, you thank them, say that was everything you needed, and end the call.
